rundown: Mountaineers beat Zips 98-60 at Hope Coliseum in Morgantown, WV. Mountaineers led 50-25 at the half and never looked back. The 2nd quarter decided it: Mountaineers won it 26-9. By ESPN's win probability it was never really in doubt (never below 99%).
Leading the way — Zips: Jessie Joaquim 14 pts; Tyla Heard 3 ast, 6 reb. Mountaineers: Skylar Forbes 21 pts; Gia Cooke 6 ast; Divine Tumba 11 reb.
Where Mountaineers won it: they shot 51% to 38%, shot 45% from three to 29% and won the boards 40-38.
Against the closing line (DraftKings): Mountaineers closed as 30.5-point favorites and covered by 7.5; the total closed at 137.5 and they combined for 158, over by 20.5.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 17, 10:26 AM ET. It had Zips 2% and Mountaineers 98%, projecting Zips 52.5 – Mountaineers 78.9 (131.4 total, Mountaineers by 26.3).

Final: Zips 60 – Mountaineers 98. Right winner: it had Mountaineers at 98%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Zips came in with a 5% below average attack and a league-average defense (1-3, 62.8 scored and 65.3 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 161 and 160 games of evidence. Projected to score 52.5, they scored 60 (+7.5 points, 14% over); projected to allow 78.9, they allowed 98 (+19.1 points, 24% over).

Mountaineers came in with a 13% above average attack and a 14% stingier than average defense (4-0, 73.3 scored and 61.5 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 173 and 172 games of evidence. Projected to score 78.9, they scored 98 (+19.1 points, 24% over); projected to allow 52.5, they allowed 60 (+7.5 points, 14% over).

The bigger miss was Mountaineers' scoring (+19.1 points against projection); both sides outscored their projections, so the game ran hotter than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 158 against 131.4 projected (+26.6), about the 97th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±14).

Margin: Mountaineers by 38 against Mountaineers by 26.3 projected, about the 82nd percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±13).

An unusual result, but one the simulations saw regularly (roughly one game in six to one in twenty).

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body:

AKR ML (+4000) at +4000: the algo gave it 2% vs 2% fair (0 pts) — lost (-1u); lost to the close (closing fair chance 2%). AKR +28.5 (-110) at -110: the algo gave it 51% vs 50% fair (+0.7 pts) — lost (-1u); lost to the closing +30.5 by 2. OVER 137.5 (-110) at -110: the algo gave it 48% vs 50% fair (-1.8 pts) — won (+0.9u); same number as the close. UNDER 137.5 (-110) at -110: the algo gave it 52% vs 50% fair (+1.8 pts) — lost (-1u); same number as the close.

From the algo's snapshot to the close: spread Mountaineers -28.5 → -30.5.

No bet: nothing cleared the algo's bar before the game.

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin.

The projection missed by a lot, so those flags likely mattered here.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×1.178 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +13 points. It counts toward NCAAW scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 641 graded NCAAW games the algo now scales scoring ×0.981 and gives home teams +1.3 points. Team corrections so far: Zips attack ×0.982, defense ×0.977 (4 games); Mountaineers attack ×1.025, defense ×0.996 (4 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total outside its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
